limits.short: These are annual figures that utilities reported to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. They are not live outage data, and utilities may calculate them in different ways.

metric.noObservations: No observations are available for this metric and selection.
metric.single: Only one reported year is available; a change over time cannot be assessed.
metric.discrepancyYears: Years with duplicate or invalid observations (not plotted)
metric.meaning: These are historical system averages, not an individual household's outage experience or a prediction of its next outage. Reliability figures alone do not establish weather-related causes. Backup-power scenarios are separate, hypothetical household choices.
metric.tableNote: Not reported means missing, never zero. Entirely empty other-standard rows are hidden; customer-count-only rows remain visible. Source records are unchanged.
chart.legend: Bars show reported values. A dot on the baseline means a reported zero. A dash (-) marks a missing observation; no bar is drawn. An exclamation mark (!) indicates a reporting discrepancy. Exact values are in the yearly table below.
metric.saidiMeaning: SAIDI describes total reported interruption minutes averaged across customers over the year.
metric.saifiMeaning: SAIFI describes the reported number of sustained interruptions averaged across customers over the year. A fractional value is a system average.
metric.caidiMeaning: CAIDI describes average duration per reported customer interruption. It is not a household's total annual outage time. Missing CAIDI is not calculated from rounded SAIDI and SAIFI.
metric.scales: Each chart uses its own vertical scale. Compare years within a chart; bar heights across different metrics are not comparable.
planner.title: Outage Planner
planner.intro: What would be needed to keep a household running, and for how long? Consider electricity needs first, then an optional propane-fuel scenario.
planner.examples: Starting values are illustrative only, not measurements of any household or utility. Modify them as needed.
planner.dailyHint: Use your bill's kWh divided by its billing days. Choose a season relevant to the plan.
planner.share: Share of electricity you plan to keep using
planner.shareHint: Think about refrigeration, communications, lighting, and any essential pumps or heating equipment. This share is the estimate.
planner.daysHint: Choose a scenario, not a prediction. Historical SAIDI and CAIDI do not determine this duration.
planner.energyError: Enter nonnegative daily electricity use, an essential share from 0-100%, and an outage of at least 0.1 day. Empty or excessively large inputs cannot be calculated.
planner.energyCaption: Daily electricity share: {share}% retained (solid), {remainder}% set aside (pale).
planner.energyLimit: This is energy demand in kWh, not a generator or battery size recommendation. Equipment selection also needs simultaneous power in kW, starting surges, and system losses. No battery charging, solar production, or equipment performance is modeled here.
planner.fuelTitle: 2. Explore a generator and propane scenario (optional)
planner.fuelIntro: Fuel use is an independent assumption. Changing the electricity estimate above does not automatically change the generator burn rate below.
planner.burnHint: Use the specific generator's published consumption at the load you expect. The starting 1.0 gal/hour is only an example.
planner.hoursHint: 24 means continuous operation. Fewer hours do not establish that essential loads remain powered while it is off.
planner.fuelAssumptions: Draft assumptions: starting fuel equals 80% of nominal tank capacity; 20% of nominal capacity is held in reserve. The usable allowance is therefore 60%. These assumptions do not describe your actual tank level.
planner.tankLegend: 60% usable allowance (solid) · 20% reserve (hatched) · 20% unfilled space (pale). All percentages refer to nominal tank capacity.
planner.fuelError: Enter nonnegative fuel consumption, generator hours from 0-24, and a valid outage duration. Empty or excessively large inputs cannot be calculated.
planner.zeroFuel: No propane consumption is entered. Fuel endurance is not calculated; this does not establish electricity coverage.
planner.fuelEnough: The {days}-day scenario uses {needed} gal, leaving {balance} gal of the usable allowance. The fuel allowance covers this scenario on paper; electricity coverage is not verified.
planner.fuelShort: The {days}-day scenario needs {needed} gal-{balance} gal more than the usable allowance. The assumed fuel allowance does not cover this scenario.
planner.fuelLimit: This calculation assumes constant consumption and no deliveries during the outage. It does not verify generator output, installation, or cold-weather propane delivery capacity. Actual tank level, equipment specifications, and tank/regulator suitability need a separate check with your equipment installer and propane supplier.
planner.energyFormula: Essential kWh/day = normal kWh/day x essential share ÷ 100. Essential outage kWh = essential kWh/day x outage days. Normal outage kWh = normal kWh/day x outage days.
planner.fuelFormula: Usable gallons = nominal tank gallons x (0.80 − 0.20). Gallons/day = generator gallons/hour x hours/day + other gallons/day. Fuel required = gallons/day x outage days. Endurance = usable gallons ÷ gallons/day when consumption is greater than zero.
planner.notSaved: Draft scenarios are not saved. Reopening this page restores the illustrative values.
summary.note: Averages use consecutive calendar years for the selected state, reporting method, and major-event treatment. Missing or invalid observations are not estimated. CAIDI averages are arithmetic means of reported annual CAIDI values, not pooled interruption durations.
options.title: 3. Explore solar and battery options
options.intro: Uses the daily electricity, essential-load share, and outage duration above. Battery defaults are illustrative. Solar production and financial inputs start blank so no local production or payback is invented.
options.available: Usable capacity available at outage start (%)
options.capacityHint: Usable capacity excludes the manufacturer’s unusable portion. Available share reflects charge and any reserve you keep at outage start. Apply only delivery losses not already included in the quoted usable capacity; use 100% efficiency if it already describes energy delivered to loads.
options.powerHint: Enter manufacturer ratings and your simultaneous loads in kW. Startup demand includes other loads running at the same time. Surge duration, circuit limits, and equipment compatibility still need verification.
options.solarHint: Run PVWatts for your location and array, then enter its annual AC generation here. This draft does not call the PVWatts API or estimate production from array size alone.
options.pvwattsLink: Open PVWatts to model your array
options.productionHint: Use matching location, capacity, orientation, mounting, and loss assumptions. Consider seasonal snow losses. If you change the location or array size, update annual generation from a new model run; the planner does not rescale it.
options.selfConsumedHint: Enter a self-consumption assumption supported by load timing or a separate model. Annual generation alone cannot determine it. The remaining generation is assumed exported; fixed utility charges are not avoided.
options.zeroLoad: No essential energy demand is entered, so backup hours are not calculated. This is not a claim of unlimited backup.
options.batteryLimit: Duration assumes a constant average essential load and no recharging. It is an energy estimate, not verified backup coverage; enough kWh does not establish enough kW.
options.batteryInvalid: Enter valid household and battery assumptions: nonnegative energy, a positive outage duration, available share from 0–100%, and delivery efficiency greater than 0% and no more than 100%.
options.power.unknown: Power capability is unverified. Complete all four power inputs; surge output must be at least continuous output, and startup demand at least the running load.
options.power.insufficient: One or more entered loads exceed the entered output ratings. The energy-duration estimate does not resolve that power shortfall.
options.power.within-entered-ratings: Entered running and startup loads fit the entered output ratings. This numeric check does not verify surge duration, circuits, or equipment compatibility.
options.combinedLimit: Additional backup hours from solar are not modeled. An hourly simulation must account for sunlight, snow, load timing, battery charge/discharge limits, efficiencies, and equipment capable of operating independently of the grid.
options.solarResilience: No outage backup is assumed for solar alone. Grid-connected solar generally needs suitable equipment to operate independently during an outage; annual generation does not establish backup coverage.
options.batteryEconomics: Battery bill savings and payback are not modeled. They require tariff and operating assumptions; resilience value alone does not establish financial savings.
options.productionMissing: Enter the modeled location/source, positive array capacity, and annual generation from a location-specific model to see production results.
options.generationEquivalent: Generation as a share of annual use
options.generationLimit: Generation equivalent can exceed 100%. It is not the percentage of your bill avoided or the share of demand met at the time it occurs. The annual household reference extrapolates your daily-use input; replace a seasonal value with an annual average when assessing economics.
options.economicsMissing: To calculate savings, enter the self-consumed share (0–100%), both rates, installed cost, and annual maintenance (zero is allowed). Assumed self-consumed solar cannot exceed annual household consumption.
options.noPayback: Annual net savings are zero or negative, so there is no positive-savings simple payback.
options.economicsLimit: Annual net savings = self-consumed kWh × avoided rate + exported kWh × export rate − annual maintenance. Simple payback = installed cost ÷ positive annual net savings. This simplified calculation excludes financing, incentives, degradation, replacements, time-varying tariffs, and discounting.
options.combinedEconomics: Combined economics use the total combined cost and your entered self-consumption assumption. No extra battery arbitrage savings or improvement in self-consumption is automatically credited; hourly dispatch is not modeled.
